newsitem.title: USA: Ares-Serono gets US injunction vs generic.
newsitem.headline: Ares-Serono gets US injunction vs generic.

text.p: Ares-Serono Group's Serono Laboratories Inc said Wednesday a U.S. District Court issued a preliminary injunction barring the marketing in the U.S. of Repronex, the generic version of its infertility drug.

Serono said the U.S. District Court for the District of Columbia concluded that Repronex does not contain the same ingredients as its drug, called Pergonal, and therefore should not have been approved under an abbreviated new drug application that does not require clinical testing.
Repronex, which is distributed by Ferring Laboratories, was approved by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration in January 1997 as a generic version of Pergonal.
On May 30, Serono Laboratories challenged the FDA's approval of that application.
The company said the court indicated it had questions about the safety of Repronex, and it said the "record does not show that Repronex is a safe and effective equivalent of Pergonal."
Serono Laboratories is the U.S. member of Ares-Serono Group, a Swiss developer and marketer of pharmaceutical products.
